title: Maximum Strength of K Disjoint Subarrays
summary: Given an array of integers nums with length n and a positive odd integer k, select exactly k disjoint subarrays such that the last element of the i-th subarray appears before the first element of the (i+1)-th subarray for all 1 <= i <= k-1.
statement: Given an array of integers nums with length n and a positive odd integer k, select exactly k disjoint subarrays such that the last element of the i-th subarray appears before the first element of the (i+1)-th subarray for all 1 <= i <= k-1. The goal is to maximize the combined strength of these subarrays, defined as: strength = k × sum(sub1) - (k-1) × sum(sub2) + (k-2) × sum(sub3) - … - 2 × sum(sub{k-1}) + sum(subk) where sum(subi) is the sum of the elements in the i-th subarray. Return the maximum possible strength that can be obtained by selecting exactly k disjoint subarrays from nums.
constraints: nums is nonempty, may contain negative values, and k is a positive odd integer no larger than its length.
Choose exactly k nonempty disjoint subarrays in left-to-right order.
Subarray number i has alternating coefficient +(k-i+1) for odd i and -(k-i+1) for even i; maximize the weighted sum.
hints: At each position a selected subarray may start, continue, or a previous one may remain closed.
Track the best score after j subarrays with the current position outside or inside subarray j.
For each value and j, carry the best closed state, extend an open state, or start j from the previous j-1 state using its signed coefficient.
The two states enumerate every legal boundary choice exactly once, and restricting the final state to j=k enforces exactly k nonempty subarrays.
editorial: The two states enumerate every legal boundary choice exactly once, and restricting the final state to j=k enforces exactly k nonempty subarrays.

tests.explanation: The best single nonempty subarray is [-1], so the maximum strength is -1.
